transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with really extreme mood swings for the past year and a month. I keep shifting between periods of feeling intensely energetic, hyper, and easily irritated, and other times when I feel deeply depressed, empty, and exhausted. It has just been really hard to manage this constant back-and-forth.

Have you ever had hallucinations or strongly fixed beliefs that others said were not true when you were not in a high-energy or depressed mood episode? If so, did those symptoms last for at least 2 weeks on their own?

No, I've never experienced anything like hallucinations or beliefs that weren't real, especially not when my mood was normal. My struggles have really just been about those extreme highs and lows. I haven't had those kinds of experiences at all.

During your high-energy periods, have you ever felt that way for at least 1 week or needed hospitalization, with it causing major problems at work, school, relationships, or leading you to do risky things? Or were those periods shorter and less severely impairing?

Yes, these high-energy periods are definitely not short or mild, and they've been happening on and off for over a year. During these times, I experience extreme hyperactivity where I take on way too much work, become overly social, and have racing thoughts I just can't control. It absolutely causes major disruptions in my life rather than being a minor, short-lived phase.
During those high-energy periods, do you need much less sleep than usual and still feel rested?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't noticed a significant change in my sleep patterns during those high-energy times.
During those high-energy periods, do you feel unusually confident or powerful, like you have special abilities or can do things others can’t?
No, I don't feel like I have any special powers or feel unusually powerful. Even though I have a ton of energy and start way too many activities, I don't think I can do things that others can't.
During those high-energy periods, do you talk much more than usual or feel like you can’t stop talking?
I'm not really sure about that, to be honest. I haven't paid close attention to whether my talking habits change during those high-energy periods.
During those high-energy periods, are you much more easily distracted than usual, with your attention constantly pulled to unimportant things?
To be honest, I'm not really sure about that. I haven't noticed my attention getting easily pulled away by unimportant things during those high-energy times.

During those high-energy periods, have you done things that were unusually risky or impulsive for you, like spending too much money, unsafe sex, reckless driving, or making major decisions without thinking them through?

During those high-energy periods, I've definitely experienced a significantly increased interest and activity regarding sex. I haven't really engaged in other risky behaviors like reckless driving or wild spending sprees, though I do find myself starting way too many projects and being overly social.
During any of these high-energy periods, were you ever hospitalized, or did you have psychotic symptoms like hearing things, seeing things, or having beliefs others said were not true?
No, I have never been hospitalized during those high-energy periods. I also haven't experienced any psychotic symptoms like hearing or seeing things, or having beliefs that others said weren't true.
When one of these high-energy periods happens, does it last most of the day nearly every day for at least 1 full week?

Yes, when those high-energy periods hit, they absolutely last most of the day, nearly every day. They go on for much longer than just a single week, often persisting for weeks or even months at a time. It really feels like a constant, ongoing state of overdrive that I just can't shake.

Confirmed manic symptoms include extreme hyperactivity/increased goal-directed activity, racing thoughts, increased sociability, irritability, and increased sexual activity.
